fe_a_lesson_in_the_wilds.description: I teach every young tauren in the camp to fight, and the forest teaches better than I do. The ones from Mulgore learned in a hurry, three years ago, while they were running. They've never had to stand and hunt something that won't run from them. I'd like you to show them how it's done. Bring down Ironfur Bears in the forest, where my students can watch from the trees.
fe_a_lesson_in_the_wilds.accept_text: Take your time with them. If you finish too fast, they'll think it's easy.

fe_a_letter_for_feathermoon.description: I've written to the druid at Feathermoon Stronghold, Kindal Moonweaver, though I've never met her. She knows every plant on this coast, and I'm guessing at half of them. The Sentinels keep their distance from us, and I understand why, because we came out of nowhere. I'd still rather ask for help than lose a patient to pride. The boat to the island leaves from Feathermoon Landing on the shore, so take her my letter.
fe_a_letter_for_feathermoon.accept_text: If she asks, tell her I'm a nurse, not a healer. I don't want her expecting magic.

fe_antilus_the_soarer.description: Antilus the Soarer is the patriarch of the Frayfeather Highlands, and he's older than this roost. For as long as I've kept it, he's left our hippogryphs alone. Now he takes them out of the air, and I've lost two this month. I can't fly the highland route while he's up there. I'd hoped he'd be the one to calm the others, and he isn't going to. Bring him down, as cleanly as you can.
fe_antilus_the_soarer.accept_text: Keep the sun at your back. He likes to come out of it.

fe_bear_trouble.description: Both of my broken bones came from the same thing, a Fog Grove Ironfur. They come into the hollow at night after the smokehouse, and the settlers try to chase them off with sticks. Two men tried it this month, and I set both their legs on my kitchen table. I'd like that to be the last time I do it. Please thin the bears out before somebody tries again.
fe_bear_trouble.accept_text: They come in on the north side, where the smokehouse is. Start there, and work out into the trees.

fe_belly_hides.description: Half the refugees walked here in boots that were falling apart before they ever left Mulgore. I'm the camp's hidewright, and I've been patching the same soles for three years. What I need is soft leather, and the Lower Wilds Crocolisks have the softest belly hide in Feralas. Bring me the hides from the river. I'll have everyone shod before the wet season, the children first.
fe_belly_hides.accept_text: Cut along the sides and keep the pale belly whole. The back hide's too stiff for anything but shields.

fe_chimaeras_and_the_boats.description: The Dread Chimaeras have nested on the Isle of Dread for as long as I've been alive, and they've never once come out over the water. Now they're going for the Sentinels' boats on the way to the landing. I count them by their scales, because I can't count them in the air. Wade out over the sandbar and kill them. Bring me their scales so I know how many are left.
fe_chimaeras_and_the_boats.accept_text: They rear back before they dive. When you see one do it, get your shield up.

fe_darters_at_the_bough.description: The Dream Bough Darters were the tree's guardians, and the Dream-Touched Treants were its gardeners. Since the roots warmed, they've turned wild, and they attack anything that comes near, even me. I've sat with this tree every night since I came from Moonglade, and now I can't reach its roots. I don't want them all dead, only enough of them that I can sit with the tree again. Thin them out for me.
fe_darters_at_the_bough.accept_text: The treants are slow, and they won't follow you far. The darters will, so deal with those first.

fe_darters_at_the_roost.description: The Feralas Sprite Darters think my wind riders are rivals, and they dive at their eyes when they come in to land. Two of my riders have been thrown already, and now the mounts are starting to refuse the roost. A wind rider that won't land is no use to anybody. I've flown these routes for twenty years, and I've never had to fight off something the size of my hand. Clear the darters out of the forest round the camp.
fe_darters_at_the_roost.accept_text: They're quick, but they're not clever. Stand near the roost and they'll come to you.

fe_down_from_the_hold.description: Hadoken sent me north from Mojache after the Rage Scar yetis. They didn't leave their hold even when the worlds came together, and now they're down in the forest, angry and hungry. Some of them are singed, and yetis don't go near fire if they can help it. I'd like to know why. Kill them and bring me their fur, the singed pieces especially.
fe_down_from_the_hold.accept_text: Look at the tips of the fur. If they're burned, those are the pieces I want most.

fe_down_off_the_mountain.description: I've watched the foot of this pass for Camp Mojache for three years, and I tie a knot in this cord for everyone who comes down it. Most of them are from Mulgore, and most of them haven't eaten in days by the time they reach me. Every knot is somebody who made it over the range since the last moon. Chieftain Ahanu wants the cord at every new moon, so she knows the trail's still open and how many to cook for. Take it to her in Camp Mojache, west along the road and inside the totems.
fe_down_off_the_mountain.accept_text: Don't untie anything if it tangles. She reads those knots like a ledger, and she'll know if one's gone.

fe_fungus_that_shouldnt_be_here.description: I studied fungus at Portland State, and I never thought it'd be the most useful thing I know. There's a grey shelf fungus growing on the redwoods here that's native to the Pacific Northwest and nowhere else. It came over with the trees, which I expected. What I didn't expect is that it's showing up on the Feralas trees too, further from the groves every month. Look at the mushrooms at the edge of the groves, then go up the coast road north and tell me if they're there too.
fe_fungus_that_shouldnt_be_here.accept_text: It's grey and flat, like a plate stuck to the bark. You won't mistake it for anything that belongs here.

fe_gashtok.description: Gash'tok the Gatekeeper commands the ogres at the gate of Dire Maul, and he calls himself its lord. He wears a bent Highborne circlet, and he's huge, even for an ogre. When two of my friends and I went to look at the gate, he killed them both, and he laughed while he did it. I got away because they made sure I did. He's somewhere round the gate. I'd like you to finish what we started.
fe_gashtok.accept_text: He laughs before he swings. When you hear it, move.

fe_goldthorn_for_the_fever.description: A fever's going round the refugees' quarter now, and it's the children who've got it worst. Goldthorn brings a fever down, and I'm out of it. It likes the drier ground along the arm road, west of the camp. I've been sitting up with three of them since last night. Bring me what you can, and quickly.
fe_goldthorn_for_the_fever.accept_text: Pull it up by the base, roots and all. The leaves alone won't brew strong enough for a child.

fe_grimfang.description: Grimfang is the Woodpaw's alpha, bigger and older than the rest of them, and every scar on him is somebody else's dead hunter. You broke up his pack, and he's taken it personally. He hunts the tops of Woodpaw Hills alone now, looking for whoever did it. My father would have gone up there himself, with a spear and no armour. I'm asking you instead. Let him find you.
fe_grimfang.accept_text: He swings that spiked club wide. Stay inside the swing, and he can't get his weight behind it.

fe_guardians_of_the_ruin.description: The naga dug down to a road under Ravenwind, and now they've brought Ravenwind Guardians to hold it, up at the Ruins of Ravenwind, north of here. They've brought Ravenwind Hydras to keep it as well. My Sentinels can't get near it. If we break their hold, we can bury the road again, and that'll slow them down. Go back to the ruins and break it.
fe_guardians_of_the_ruin.accept_text: The Guardians stand on the road itself. Draw them off it one at a time, and the hydras will follow.

fe_harroks_totem.description: Pathfinder Harrok leads the Grimtotem at the compound, and he wears a totem on his belt like a trophy. It was carved for the Bloodhoof lodge before I was born, and a woman carried it out of Thunder Bluff on her back. She didn't survive the Needles. Harrok found her pack where she fell, and he's worn her totem ever since. He doesn't go far from the Grimtotem Compound, north-west of the camp, so bring it back to us.
fe_harroks_totem.accept_text: Take him down quickly, before he works out what you've come for and breaks it to spite you.

fe_highland_nests.description: I want to know whether the wild hippogryphs of the Frayfeather Highlands have left their nests or only their manners. They nest on the crags up on the highlands. If they've left the nests, something big has frightened them, and I'll have to keep my mounts on the island. If they're still there, I can work round it. Go and look, and don't touch the eggs.
fe_highland_nests.accept_text: Stay low on the crags and move slowly. A parent on the nest thinks anything quick is a hunter.

fe_hydras_on_sardor.description: The naga keep Sardor Hydras on the isle like hounds, and they've started loosing them on the sandbar at night. Each one has three heads, and every head bites. My Sentinels can't hold the bar while those things are on it. I lost a good bow to one last night, and very nearly the arm that holds it. Kill them on Sardor Isle.
fe_hydras_on_sardor.accept_text: Watch all three heads, not just the one looking at you. It's the other two that bite.

fe_into_the_hive.description: The line of mounds ends at a hive mouth in the Hive Fields, and Orwin's calling it the Zukk'ash Hive. I've had enough of things coming up out of the ground under my camp. I didn't bring these people out of the Needles to have them eaten in their beds. Go down into the hive and kill its Hive Warriors and its Ravagers. Take friends, because Hadoken says it goes down a long way.
fe_into_the_hive.accept_text: Mark the walls as you go down. Hadoken's hunters say every gallery in there looks the same.

fe_khadgars_whisker.description: The refugees brought a coughing sickness out of the Needles, and it's going round the whole camp now. Khadgar's Whisker settles the lungs, and I ran out of it a week ago. I'm brewing tea in every pot the inn will lend me, and it still isn't enough. The Whisker grows wild along the river in the Lower Wilds and in the clearings of the forest. Bring me what you can find.
fe_khadgars_whisker.accept_text: Pick the ones with the white tips. They're the strongest, and they dry the fastest.

fe_lady_szaressa.description: Lady Szaressa commands the Hatecrest at the Ruins of Ravenwind, north of here, and the Guardians answer to her. When she's hurt, she wraps herself in a ward of sea water, and my arrows just bounce off it. I've watched her shrug off a whole volley. Everything they've dug up on this coast passes through her hands. Break the ward and finish her.
fe_lady_szaressa.accept_text: The ward doesn't last. Keep hitting it, and when it breaks, don't give her time to call it back.

fe_lotus_for_the_draughts.description: I brew the healing draughts for the Sentinels on the walls, and since the naga came, they've gone through them faster than I can brew. Sungrass is the base of every one. It grows in the open, on the highlands and up the north coast. I've stripped every patch within a day's walk of the stronghold. Bring me what you can find further out.
fe_lotus_for_the_draughts.accept_text: Pick it in the morning if you can. Sungrass picked after noon goes bitter by the time it reaches me.

fe_makrura_for_the_pot.description: I feed the Sentinels on nightfin and makrura, and the makrura on the beaches have come up fat and bold since the naga arrived. I think the naga feed them. They've got the sweetest tail meat on the coast. The Sentinels are tired of my soup, and they've started telling me so. Bring me some tails from the Hatecrest Makrura on the Hatecrest Shore, north of here.
fe_makrura_for_the_pot.accept_text: Cut the tail off at the last joint. That's where the meat is, and the rest is shell.

fe_makrura_on_the_beach.description: The Hatecrest Makrura come up on the shore ahead of the naga, like scouts. They snap at anything that lands, and our fishing boats can't get ashore at the landing any more. They come off the Hatecrest Shore, north of here. Elyssa's nets have sat dry for a week, and the Sentinels are living on soup. I'd rather they weren't. Clear the makrura off the beaches.
fe_makrura_on_the_beach.accept_text: Come at them from the land side. They watch the water, not the trees.

fe_meat_for_the_winter.description: I keep Cedar Hollow fed through the wet season, and the wet season here goes on a long time. I logged out of Forks for thirty years and hunted elk every fall, so I know what I'm doing with one. The Fog Grove Elk came over with the trees, and there are more of them every year. I won't cut these trees, but I'll hunt the elk that came with them. Bring me good cuts, and the hollow eats this winter.
fe_meat_for_the_winter.accept_text: Shoulder and haunch, and bleed them quick. I'll smoke whatever you bring the same night.

fe_medicine_by_the_creek.description: I was an ER nurse in Tacoma, and in Cedar Hollow I'm the only one there is. My pharmacy is whatever grows by the creek. Right now I've got two people with broken bones and a man who won't stop coughing. The night elves taught me that Purple Lotus makes a decent painkiller if you boil it right. It grows along the creeks and the coast, so bring me what you can find.
fe_medicine_by_the_creek.accept_text: Take the whole flower and some of the stem. The night elves swear the stem's where the good part is.

fe_more_bedrolls_than_beds.description: For three years I've had people sleeping on the floor of my inn and under bare poles behind it. The rain comes straight through the lean-tos in the refugees' quarter, and the old ones have started to cough. An Ironfur Bear's pelt sheds water like a roof, and those bears are the warmest thing in Feralas. Bring me their pelts from the forest. I'll have them stitched into blankets before the next storm comes in off the coast.
fe_more_bedrolls_than_beds.accept_text: Skin them whole if you can. A pelt full of holes is just a wet rug.

fe_mounds_in_the_forest.description: A few months ago, mounds of raw earth started pushing up through the forest floor south of the camp, toward the Hive Fields. Last night I watched Zukk'ash Swarmers come up out of one mound and go down into another. They had far too many legs. I didn't sleep after that, and I don't think I'm going to tonight. Go and look at the mounds, and kill whatever comes out of them.
fe_mounds_in_the_forest.accept_text: Stand back from the mounds when you look. The ground round them is hollow, and it gives.

fe_night_diggers.description: I watch the coast from Feathermoon to Sardor Isle, and I've been watching the Hatecrest Ruin-Diggers for a month. They come up the beaches at night with picks and sacks, and they're careful. Whatever they find, they wrap in kelp, like it's precious, and carry it back to the sea. Naga don't treat anything gently, so it must matter to someone. Take it off them on the Hatecrest Shore and bring it to me.
fe_night_diggers.accept_text: Don't unwrap the kelp. I want to see it the way they packed it.

fe_ogres_in_the_dome.description: The Gordunni at the Ruins of Isildien, north-east of here, are working in shifts. The Isildien Diggers work the archive stair, and the Brutes stand over them while they do. Every day they're down there, they break into another room of the archive. Some of those rooms haven't been opened in ten thousand years, and I'd hoped to be the one who opened them. Please stop them before there's nothing left to open.
fe_ogres_in_the_dome.accept_text: Kill them on the stair if you can, and try not to bring the walls down doing it.

fe_ogres_on_the_arm_road.description: I keep Orgrimmar's eye on Camp Mojache, and lately it's been on the Gordunni. They've built a forward outpost west of the gate, and their Brutes have started stopping anything on the road to the coast. The Shamans with them aren't stupid, either, and that worries me more than the Brutes do. A camp this size lives or dies by its caravans. Break up the outpost and keep the road open.
fe_ogres_on_the_arm_road.accept_text: Take the Shamans down before they get their totems planted. A Brute's just a Brute without them.

fe_old_grizzlegut.description: Old Grizzlegut is an Ironfur the size of a lodge, and he's been fishing the Lower Wilds since before Mojache had a palisade. He's killed two of Hadoken's hunters, and Hadoken wants him gone from the river. I want his pelt, because it would keep a family warm for twenty years. He's down in the marsh where the river pools. I'd come with you, but I'm a lot more use with a knife once he's down.
fe_old_grizzlegut.accept_text: He stands up before he charges. When he does, get out of the way, and don't try to hold your ground.

fe_old_seven_point.description: Old Seven-Point came through with the trees, same as we did. He's a Roosevelt bull, bigger than any elk I ever saw in Washington, and he leads the herd in the Fog Groves. This season he's charged three of us, and last week he put Sam in the creek. I've hunted elk every fall for thirty years, and I've never had one come looking for me. He'll be somewhere in the groves, bugling, so you'll hear him before you see him.
fe_old_seven_point.accept_text: He drops his head before he comes. When it goes down, you've got about two seconds.

fe_orders_for_the_watch.description: I need to know whether the Hatecrest are digging at Ravenwind, on the north coast, as well. The Sentinels' Watch is as far north as Feathermoon reaches, and Sentinel Aerwyn Starbrook holds it. We haven't heard from her in weeks, which isn't like her. Take my orders north up the coast road to her. If the naga are digging there too, I need to know before they find what they're looking for.
fe_orders_for_the_watch.accept_text: Don't stop at Ravenwind on the way. Get to the Watch first, and let Aerwyn tell you what's there.

fe_pages_from_the_dome.description: The ogres carried books out of the archive, and their Ogre Mages read the pages aloud to each other, badly. I've listened from the rubble, and they understand a little more of it every night. A Highborne archivist would have wept to hear it, and I very nearly did. I want those pages back before they understand the rest. Bring me every page you can take off the mages at the Ruins of Isildien, north-east of here.
fe_pages_from_the_dome.accept_text: Don't fold them. The ink's older than anything else on this coast, and it cracks.

fe_raise_it_here.description: I've raised the Bloodhoof totem beside Mojache's great totem. Raising it here means we've stopped waiting to go home. I didn't think I'd ever be ready for that, and I'm still not sure I am. I want the camp to see someone from outside it standing with us, so they know it isn't only the refugees who mourn. Come and stand with us at the great totem tonight.
fe_raise_it_here.accept_text: Come to the great totem tonight. You don't have to say anything, only stand with us.

fe_ravenwinds_diggers.description: The Hatecrest who came up with the merge are digging at the Ruins of Ravenwind, the same way they've been digging down by Feathermoon. Their Sea Witches call up the tide to wash the earth away from the old stones, and their Raiders guard them while they do. I've got six Sentinels to hold this whole stretch of coast, and none to spare for a ruin. I want them stopped before they're finished. Go north up the coast and break up the digging.
fe_ravenwinds_diggers.accept_text: Kill the Sea Witches before the tide comes in. Once the water's up, you'll be fighting knee deep.

fe_report_to_orgrimmar.description: I've written up everything about the Gordunni and the gate of Dire Maul, and it needs to go to Elder Torgun in Orgrimmar. He sits in the Valley of Wisdom, and he remembers the old stories about the city in Feralas. I don't, and I've stopped pretending I do. Tell him the chains face inward. He'll know what that means better than I do.
fe_report_to_orgrimmar.accept_text: Take a wind rider from Shyn's roost, and don't stop to rest until the report's in his hands.

fe_resin_for_sale.description: I came to Feralas to buy silithid resin, and I'm still buying. The Zukk'ash Tunnelers coat their tunnels with it as they dig, and the engineers in Gadgetzan pay a fortune for it. It's about the only thing that still sells, since you newcomers turned the whole market upside down. Here's the odd part, though. I weigh every lump, and the grit in it's been changing. Bring me a good batch from the Hive Fields, and I'll pay like always.
fe_resin_for_sale.accept_text: Usual rate, no haggling. Keep the lumps whole, because I weigh the grit, and powder tells me nothing.

fe_sardor_isle.description: The Hatecrest have taken Sardor Isle, off the north-west shore, and turned it into their camp on this coast. Their Coral Guardians hold the sandbar, and their Tide Priestesses keep the camp. You can wade across the sandbar at low tide, which is how they get back and forth. Every raid on our beaches starts from that island. Wade across and break the camp.
fe_sardor_isle.accept_text: Go at low tide and be back before it turns. The bar's under water by nightfall.

fe_show_the_druid.description: I've sealed my spore samples in a jar with wax, so nothing gets out on the way. They need to go to Kindal Moonweaver at Feathermoon Stronghold, on the island. Rosa says she's the one who knows what the old forest can survive. I'm not worried about the groves, because they're used to this fungus. I'm worried about the old forest round them, and she'll understand the difference.
fe_show_the_druid.accept_text: Keep the jar upright and out of the sun. If the wax cracks, bring it straight back to me.

fe_skull_taker_murg.description: Skull-Taker Murg leads the Gordunni at the Ruins of Isildien, and he takes a skull from everyone he kills. He wears them on his belt. Two of them are my sisters'. I've asked the General to let me go after him, and she says no, because I'd go alone. So I'm asking you instead.
fe_skull_taker_murg.accept_text: He walks the dome at Isildien. When he's down, bring me the belt, and don't look too closely at it.

fe_smoked_elk_for_the_inn.description: Every Sentinel who walks past the transplants' hollow comes back talking about the smell from that smokehouse. I'm told a settler named Walt Hollis smokes the best elk on the coast. I've never spoken to a settler in my life, but I keep an inn, and an inn needs meat. I'd like to trade, my wine for his elk. Take him my offer in Cedar Hollow.
fe_smoked_elk_for_the_inn.accept_text: Be polite with him. I'm told he's a proud man, and I'd rather we didn't start badly.

fe_snares_on_the_trail.description: The Woodpaw Trappers have been setting snares on our hunting trails, and last week one of them caught a refugee girl by the ankle. Her ankle will heal, and my temper won't. The trappers carry their snares on their belts up in Woodpaw Hills. Take every one off them and bring them to me. I'm going to burn them where the gnolls can see the smoke.
fe_snares_on_the_trail.accept_text: Watch your own feet on the way up. They hide the loops under the leaf litter, right on the trail.

fe_spears_at_the_wind_riders.description: The Grimtotem at the compound have started throwing spears at anything that flies over them. Their Pathfinders throw, and their Earthbreakers cheer them on. Last week they brought down one of my wind riders. I found her in the trees the next morning, with the spear still in her wing. I'd like her to be the last. Clear them out of the Grimtotem Compound, north-west of the camp.
fe_spears_at_the_wind_riders.accept_text: The Pathfinders keep to the high ground, where they've got a clear throw. Go up after them.

fe_spores_on_the_hides.description: I think the animals are carrying the spores, and that's why it's spreading so fast. The Feralas Stalkers range further than anything else in the groves, so they're my first suspect. If I'm right, their fur will be full of grey spores. Bring me fur from the stalkers and I'll look at it under my lens. It's the only one on this side of the world, and I traded Walt a month of firewood for it.
fe_spores_on_the_hides.accept_text: Pull the fur from the back of the neck. That's what brushes against the bark when they climb.

fe_stalkers_in_the_fog.description: The Feralas Stalkers have learned that we walk the groves in the fog, and that we can't see far in it. Back home we had cougars, and you learned to make yourself big and loud. These cats don't care how big you are. They've taken two of Walt's goats, and last week they followed Rosa home. She didn't sleep that night, and she's the one who keeps the rest of us alive. Hunt them out of the groves for me.
fe_stalkers_in_the_fog.accept_text: They circle before they jump. If the fog goes quiet around you, turn round.

fe_stalkers_on_the_north_coast.description: Since the merge, the Feralas Stalkers have spread up the coast. They come out of the Fog Groves, east of here, and now they've followed the yetis' scent up the coast, and they hunt the coast road between the Forgotten Coast and the Sentinels' Watch. My runners won't take it alone any more, and I don't blame them. Last week one of them came in with claw marks right through her pack. Clear the road through the Twin Colossals.
fe_stalkers_on_the_north_coast.accept_text: They hunt the road at dusk. Walk it then, and they'll come to you.

fe_tell_moonglade.description: I've written to Dreamwatcher Lethiel at Moonglade's Dreaming Arch. The roots are warm, the guardians are dreaming badly, and the giants are walking. She needs to hear all of it, and soon. I can't leave the Bough while it's like this. Take her my letter, and she'll know what it means, or she'll know who to ask.
fe_tell_moonglade.accept_text: Lethiel sits with the Dreaming Arch in Moonglade's north woods. Take her my letter.

fe_the_crossed_off_names.description: I've started a second page, for the names I've crossed off. Three hunters went down to the Lower Wilds in the first winter to feed the camp, and none of them came back. I put them on that page, but I never found out how they died. Their families still ask me, and I've got nothing to tell them. Search the riverbank for me, and if the Lower Wilds Crocolisks are what took them, make the river safer for the next ones.
fe_the_crossed_off_names.accept_text: Look in the mud along the bank. A hunter carries his spear everywhere, and a spear doesn't rot.

fe_the_crossing.description: I keep the pier at Feathermoon Landing, and I decide who gets on the boat. The Sentinels let transplants land on the island now, but only the ones I've watched for a while. I've watched you. Take this moon token, and the crew will let you aboard with it. Shandris Feathermoon stands in front of the great hall, and she'll know I sent you.
fe_the_crossing.accept_text: She's busy, so don't waste her time. Say who sent you, then let her talk.

fe_the_deep_mother.description: The hunters who've seen the hive's queen call her the Deep Mother, and I can't say I've got a better name. Her chamber's where the main gallery of the Zukk'ash Hive levels out, a long way down, south of the camp. She lays the eggs, and the whole hive does whatever she wants. Kill her, and the hive stops growing. I'll still buy the resin, mind, so don't go burning it all.
fe_the_deep_mother.accept_text: Bring friends who can take a beating, and don't go down there tired.

fe_the_dig_head.description: Past the Deep Mother's chamber, the Zukk'ash are still digging. A silithid the size of a kodo stands at the head of the dig and drives the workers on, and the hunters call it Tunnelmaster Zix'tal. They heard it from the far end of the Zukk'ash Hive, south of here, and they say it doesn't sound like the forest down there any more. A tunnel that long is going somewhere, and I'd like to know where before it gets there. Kill the thing and see where they were digging.
fe_the_dig_head.accept_text: Notice the air when you get down there. If it's dry, tell me, and I'll know what it means.

fe_the_diggers.description: I've laid the naga's relics and the ogres' pages side by side, and they point to the same place. The naga are digging up the old roads, the ogres are digging up the archive, and both of them are looking for the way into Eldre'Thalas. Your Horde has a man at Camp Mojache who watches the gate. Take him my notes, from someone who's seen both. For once, the Sentinels and the Horde want the same thing.
fe_the_diggers.accept_text: He's an orc, and he'll want it short. Tell him the naga and the ogres are after the same door.

fe_the_gate.description: The Gordunni hold the Gate of Dire Maul, west of here in the middle of the arm, and they've barricaded it with tree trunks and chains. I want to know whether they're keeping people out or keeping something in. You can only tell by getting close and seeing which way the chains face. Their Maulers and Warlords guard it day and night, so you'll have to go through them. Look at the barricade properly, and come back and tell me.
fe_the_gate.accept_text: Chains on the outside mean they're keeping us out. On the inside, it's worse, so look carefully.

fe_the_hatecrest_shore.description: Since the merge, the Hatecrest naga have come up onto the beaches north of the landing, and they come at night. Their Raiders hold the sand, and their Ruin-Diggers aren't fighting at all, they're digging. The naga have raided this coast before, but in all the years I've held it, they've never once stopped to dig. This morning I counted eleven fresh holes below the landing. I want to know why, but first I want them off my coast.
fe_the_hatecrest_shore.accept_text: Hit the Raiders first. The Diggers won't stop to help them, which tells you how much the digging matters.

fe_the_hippogryphs_are_restless.description: The wild hippogryphs of the Frayfeather Highlands have turned on our patrols, and they've never attacked a Sentinel before. The Skystalkers and Windwings dive at every patrol on the highlands now. I think something's driving them, and I mean to find out what. For now, though, the patrols need the sky clear. Thin them before someone's killed.
fe_the_hippogryphs_are_restless.accept_text: Don't chase the ones that flee. I only need them wary, not gone.

fe_the_list.description: I keep the list of everyone who reached Mojache, and everyone they're still looking for. Elder Longtread has kept his own list at Camp Taurajo since the fall, and nobody's ever put the two side by side. Some of the names I'm looking for might be on his, and some of his might be here. I've copied mine out in my best hand. Ride it to him at Camp Taurajo if you can, because some of these people have waited three years.
fe_the_list.accept_text: If he asks who wrote it, tell him Brann Tallgrass. He knew my father, and he'll read it faster for that.

fe_the_nine_names.description: Forty of us walked out of Mulgore together, and thirty-one reached Mojache. I say the other nine names every night, at the memorial pole on the north-west side of camp, in the refugees' quarter. Every token on that pole is somebody who didn't get here. I'd like someone who wasn't with us to stand where I stand, and then walk out to the bottom of the pass, where we came down. See both before I tell you anything more.
fe_the_nine_names.accept_text: Start at the pole, then go out to the pass. Take your time on the walk between them.

fe_the_old_bull.description: The Rage Scar Old Bull leads what's left of the yetis, and he's stopped running. He attacks anything that moves now. Yesterday he threw one of the Sentinels into a tree, and she still can't lift her arm. I've hunted angry animals before, and the old ones are always the worst. He's somewhere round Rage Scar Hold, in the forest to the north. End it for him.
fe_the_old_bull.accept_text: He'll charge the moment he sees you. Let him come, and step aside at the last moment.

fe_the_old_walker.description: The Old Walker is the eldest of the giants under the Twin Colossals, older than Feathermoon itself. For as long as anyone remembers, he stood still. Now he walks, the ground shakes under him, and my hippogryphs won't fly within a mile of the north coast. I've lost the whole route, and the Watch is cut off from the sky. Please stop him.
fe_the_old_walker.accept_text: He's slow, but every step knocks you off your feet. Don't stand where he's about to walk.

fe_the_rattles_go_quiet.description: With their snares gone, the Woodpaw have pulled back to their camps, and their Woodpaw Mystics are shaking their rattles all night. I know what that means, because I've heard it before. They're working themselves up to come back. When the Mystics start rattling, the Woodpaw Brutes come down the hill a night later. I'd rather we went up into Woodpaw Hills, north of the camp, first.
fe_the_rattles_go_quiet.accept_text: Break up the camp before they're ready.

fe_the_road_under_ravenwind.description: The naga dug down to an old Highborne road under Ravenwind, and it runs inland. I want to see where it actually goes. Find it in the Ruins of Ravenwind, north of here, and follow it inland as far as the Twin Colossals. I've got a guess, and I don't like it. If it goes where I think it does, Latronicus needs to know.
fe_the_road_under_ravenwind.accept_text: Stay on the old stones as you follow it. Where the road goes under the grass, look for the line of the kerbs.

fe_through_to_the_other_side.description: The Zukk'ash tunnel comes out in the Dry Deep, under the Abyssal Sands. The Dark Iron of Onyxhollow live below it, and they ought to know somebody's dug a road to their door. I've written their geomancer a letter, and I think it's polite. Walk the tunnel past where Zix'tal was digging, and you'll come out in the Dry Deep. Onyxhollow's at the end of the descent, and the letter's for Vigdis Stonesong.
fe_through_to_the_other_side.accept_text: Be polite, she's a dwarf. Hand it over before you tell her a goblin wrote it.

fe_tidelord_ssaravel.description: Tidelord Ssaravel commands the Hatecrest on Sardor Isle, and he's the one with the maps. Every map we've taken off the priestesses was copied from his. With his own maps in my hands, I'd know what they're digging for and where they'll dig next. He calls up the sea when he's cornered, so watch your footing. He'll be on the isle.
fe_tidelord_ssaravel.accept_text: When the water starts rising round your ankles, get to higher ground. He'll follow you up.

fe_trees_that_dont_answer.description: I've watched the Fog Groves from the walls for two years, and I've tried speaking to the trees. Every tree in Feralas knows its own name and will tell you, if you know how to ask. The trees in the groves don't answer at all. I want to know how the old forest is taking them, and how it's taking the people who came with them. Go and stand among the redwoods, then visit Cedar Hollow, where the settlers live.
fe_trees_that_dont_answer.accept_text: Don't tell the settlers I sent you. I'd rather hear how they are when nobody's watching.

fe_twice_the_mouths.description: Camp Mojache was built for half the tauren who live in it now. When the first refugees walked in out of the Needles, I didn't count them, I just opened the gate. Now I count every meal, and the count never comes out in our favour. The Feralas Stags in the forest round the camp are the best meat we've got. Hunt them, and bring the haunches to Wahya at the cook fires.
fe_twice_the_mouths.accept_text: Wahya's the one stirring the biggest pot. She'll take the haunches off you before you've put them down.

fe_vouching_for_the_hollow.description: I've decided to speak for Cedar Hollow to the General. Until she agrees, the settlers need something to show any Sentinel who troubles them. This is the Sentinels' mark. If a patrol stops them, they show it, and the Sentinel walks away. Take it to June Nakamura in Cedar Hollow, and tell her I'll keep my word.
fe_vouching_for_the_hollow.accept_text: Give it to June and nobody else. She's the one the others listen to.

fe_walkers_under_the_arches.description: The Colossal Land Walkers and Sea Walkers have stood under the Twin Colossals since before the night elves came to this forest. Now they've started walking toward the Bough, and they trample everything in their way. I don't know what they mean to do when they get there. I'd rather not find out. Stop them under the arches south of here, before they get any closer.
fe_walkers_under_the_arches.accept_text: The Sea Walkers keep to the water's edge, and the Land Walkers to the high ground. You'll need both.

fe_warm_roots.description: I came from Moonglade to the Dream Bough, a great tree whose roots reach into the Dream. They've been restless since the merge. The stones of the Dreaming Arch at Moonglade have been warm at night for months, and the Bough's roots touch the same Dream. I want to know whether these roots are warm too. Go and lay your hand on them tonight, and tell me.
fe_warm_roots.accept_text: Lay your hand on the Bough's roots tonight, and tell me whether they're warm.

fe_watch_fires.description: I keep the harbour, and I'm the one who lights the signal fire when the Watch in the north sends word. The Watch lights a fire on the cliffs when it needs us, and I light ours to answer. It's been dark for a month. Go up the coast road to the Sentinels' Watch and see they're all right. Then look under the Colossals on your way back, because that's where the last fire was.
fe_watch_fires.accept_text: If they're in trouble, don't try to fix it yourself. Come back and tell me, and I'll bring the boats.

fe_what_drove_them.description: Something's driven the chimaeras out of their nests, and I want to know what. They nest on the old Highborne tower at the heart of the Isle of Dread. The Dread Matriarch guards those nests, and she's never left them before. If she leaves now, she'll take the young ones with her and nest somewhere worse. Cross the sandbar, look at the tower, and make sure she's gone before that happens.
fe_what_drove_them.accept_text: Look at the ground round the tower as well as the nests. Whatever drove them out came from somewhere.

fe_what_drove_them_out.description: Every yeti I've looked at is singed at the tips, so something hot drove them out of Rage Scar Hold. I want someone to look inside the hold itself. It's up in the east hills, and the Rage Scar Matriarchs are still guarding the mouth. They won't let you past easily. Go in and tell me what you see.
fe_what_drove_them_out.accept_text: Look at the back wall, not just the floor. If something came in, it didn't come through the front.

fe_what_i_owe_them.description: There's a stump behind the hollow, and I'm the one who made it. I cut that tree the first week, for the cabin, before I'd worked out where I was. It's a redwood, maybe four hundred years old, and it was one of the only ones on a whole continent. I haven't cut a single tree since, and I never will. Go and look at that stump, and then come back and tell me I'm a sentimental old fool.
fe_what_i_owe_them.accept_text: It's behind the smokehouse, under the moss. You'll have to look for it, because I let it grow over.

fe_what_isildien_was.description: I keep the record of the Highborne ruins on this coast, and it's been a busy record since the merge. The Ruins of Isildien are the biggest of them. Isildien was a library before the Sundering, the largest outside the capital, and the dome's still standing, just about. Now the Gordunni are digging it out. Go and look at what the ogres are doing to it, and come back and tell me how bad it is.
fe_what_isildien_was.accept_text: Look at the stairs. Whichever way they've dug down will tell me what they're after.

fe_what_the_grimtotem_took.description: While we were burying our dead in Mulgore, the Grimtotem moved onto the empty ground in Feralas. The Grimtotem Compound north of the arm road was Mojache's hunting camp before the merge, with the old lodges and the springs. Their Usurpers took it, and their Bonecallers hex anyone who comes near the water. They turn our refugees away at spearpoint, tauren turning away tauren. Drive them back from it.
fe_what_the_grimtotem_took.accept_text: Kill the Bonecallers first. A hex doesn't wear off while its caster is still chanting.

fe_what_the_mages_carry.description: Every Gordunni Ogre Mage I've killed had a scroll on him, half burned. Ogres can barely read their own names, so somebody's teaching them, or they're copying something out. I don't like not knowing which. The mages work at the outpost and round the Gate of Dire Maul, west of here. Kill them and bring me what they're carrying.
fe_what_the_mages_carry.accept_text: Grab the scrolls before they finish burning. They put a light to them when they know they're losing.

fe_where_the_line_goes.description: Orwin marked every mound he knows of on a map, then put a ruler on it, and they all fall on the same line. Silithids don't dig in straight lines unless they're going somewhere. I want to know where. Walk the line through the Hive Fields for me, mound by mound. Tell me what's at the end of it.
fe_where_the_line_goes.accept_text: Follow the mounds, not the swarmers. The swarmers wander, and the line doesn't.

fe_which_trees_these_are.description: I was a ranger in Olympic National Park for sixteen years, and I know every tree in these groves by name. The big ones with the soft red bark are coast redwoods, and the dark ones are Sitka spruce. On Earth they only ever grew on the Pacific coast of North America. Here they've come up in the middle of Feralas, and I need fresh eyes on how they sit beside the old forest. Walk the north edge of the Fog Groves, then go into the heart of them, and look at where ours stop and Feralas starts.
fe_which_trees_these_are.accept_text: Touch the bark if you like. Redwood's soft, almost spongy, and you'll know it the moment you feel it.

fe_windwings_over_the_arches.description: The Frayfeather Windwings have come down off the Frayfeather Highlands, north-east of here, to the Twin Colossals, and they're nesting on top of the arches. They dive at anything that walks underneath. Our patrols to the Watch go right under them, and I've had two Sentinels come back bleeding from the scalp. I don't care why they're up there, I need the patrols to get through. Drive them off the arches.
fe_windwings_over_the_arches.accept_text: Shoot them as they dive, not while they're perched. They're slower coming down.

fe_wolves_on_the_trail.description: The Longtooth Runners have worked out that the people coming down off the mountain are exhausted, and they hunt the bottom of the pass now. I've buried two travellers this season who made it over the whole range and died a mile from the camp. One of them still had his pack on, with a letter inside for somebody in Mojache. I'd like those wolves to learn that the bottom of this trail isn't easy hunting any more. Thin them out where the descent levels off, and don't stop until they think twice.
fe_wolves_on_the_trail.accept_text: They lie up in the long grass where the descent levels off. Keep your back to the rocks.

fe_woodpaw_in_the_hills.description: I keep this camp fed, and since the merge doubled it, the Woodpaw have been raiding my hunting grounds. Their Reavers come down out of the hills north-east of Mojache with their hyenas and take whatever my hunters bring down. Last week they took a whole stag off two of my boys and left them to walk home with nothing. They've worked out that we're feeding more people, and they think that makes us soft. Go up into Woodpaw Hills and show them otherwise.
fe_woodpaw_in_the_hills.accept_text: Kill the hyenas when you can. A Reaver without his dogs turns round and goes home.

fe_word_to_hadoken.description: Hadoken sent me north, and he'll want to know what I found at Rage Scar Hold. Something came up from underneath it, through the back wall, the same way the silithids came up under the forest at home. It's the strangest thing I've seen since the merge. I'd go myself, but somebody has to keep watch on the hold. Tell him it came from underneath, and he'll know to watch the ground.
fe_word_to_hadoken.accept_text: He'll be at the hunters' fire in Mojache. Tell him straight, because he hates it when people dress things up.
